fields.summary: Replace legacy \curl with \core\http_client (Guzzle)

issuetype.description: A big user story that needs to be broken down. Created by Jira Software - do not edit or delete.
issuetype.name: Epic

components.name: Other
components.description: Issues that don't fit anywhere else

fields.description:
h2. Summary

Moodle's legacy {{\curl}} class ({{lib/filelib.php}}, together with {{\curl_cache}}) is to be replaced by {{\core\http_client}} (Guzzle). Guzzle is already used by newer subsystems (Communication, the outbound MoodleNet integration, AI). The remaining {{\curl}} usage in core will be migrated, and {{\curl}} is deprecated early so that product teams, certified partners, and the wider community have as much time as possible to react.

h3. Scope

* Initial deprecation of {{\curl}} (and {{\curl_cache}}) on the main branch, as early as possible, per our deprecation policy.
* Advance notice to product teams, certified partners, and the wider community by MoodleHQ, as early as possible.
* All direct core usages of {{\curl}} are replaced with {{\core\http_client}}.
* {{\curl}} is rewritten internally as a thin wrapper over {{\core\http_client}}, so that all requests go through Guzzle even while legacy code still runs.
* Current feature gaps relative to Guzzle will be closed (e.g., multipart upload of {{stored_file}} objects via {{stored_file::add_to_curl_request()}}).
* OAuth2: a new Guzzle-based OAuth2 client is introduced alongside the existing {{\oauth2_client}} and  {{\core\oauth2\client}}. The legacy classes are deprecated and removed, along with {{\curl}}, in a single major release, likely after the policy minimum.

h3. Out of scope

* Bundled third-party libraries using {{\curl}}: phpFlickr, Google API client IO adapter, SimplePie integration, LTI provider
* The PHP cURL extension itself and usages of native {{curl_*}} functions.

fields.summary: Ad-hoc task mod_qbank\task\transfer_question_categories causes performance issues on large sites

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
Due to some (unknown) bug that causes massive question duplication, we have millions of question copies. There’s one question category with 1.070.303 questions.

The ad-hoc task {{mod_qbank\task\transfer_question_categories}} goes through all top question categories and calls {{qbank_managecategories\helper::question_remove_stale_questions_from_category}} for every sub-category. This loads ALL questions into RAM, which are either old-style random questions (qtype = random) or any questions that were deleted while they were in use by a quiz (status = hidden), but whose usages have since been removed.

{code:sql}SELECT q.id
FROM mdl_question q
  JOIN mdl_question_versions qv ON qv.questionid = q.id
  JOIN mdl_question_bank_entries qbe ON qbe.id = qv.questionbankentryid
WHERE qbe.questioncategoryid = :categoryid
  AND (q.qtype = 'random' OR qv.status = 'hidden');{code}

Then, {{question_delete_question()}} is called on every question. This creates another couple of dozen SELECT and DELETE statements for every question. We can roughly delete 500 questions per minute. This takes way too long to comb through 15 million questions.

Running the following query

{code:sql}SELECT qbe.questioncategoryid, count(qbe.questioncategoryid) as numberofquestions
FROM mdl_question q
         JOIN mdl_question_versions qv ON qv.questionid = q.id
         JOIN mdl_question_bank_entries qbe ON qbe.id = qv.questionbankentryid
WHERE (q.qtype = 'random' OR qv.status = 'hidden')
GROUP BY qbe.questioncategoryid
HAVING numberofquestions > 10000
ORDER BY numberofquestions DESC;{code}

gives me 68 question categories with between 1.071.300 and 10.257 questions each. That’s 15.064.429 questions combined from a total of 16.962.840 questions.



We need to make this more efficient.

fields.summary: Restoring course backup causes Essay questions with response template to save empty answers

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
Description:

Normally when using a response template in an Essay question, if a student leaves the question blank (with only the template text), it will register as ‘Not yet answered’ on the summary page when reaching the end of the Quiz. However, when backing up and restoring the course, this behaviour changes to ‘Answer saved’ when no additional text (beyond the template) is present. This is replicable in sandbox.moodledemo.net

Steps to replicate:

# Create a test course
# Enrol a Student user
# Create a new Quiz activity
# Add an Essay question
# Give the question a name and Question text
# Under ‘Response template’ paste the following text: 

{quote}Here is a response template



Please answer in 25 words or less whether restoring this to a new course will cause this question to be automatically flagged as 'Answer saved'{quote}

# Save the question
# Log in as the Student
# Attempt the quiz - During the Essay question do not enter any additional text, simply click ‘Finish attempt…’
# On the ‘Summary of attempt’ screen, note that it displays ‘Not yet answered’:
!image-20250908-065633.png|width=1199,height=808,alt="image-20250908-065633.png"!
# Log back in as an admin
# Go to the course, then More>Course reuse
# Back up the course in full
# Restore as a new course
# Enrol a new test Student
# Repeat steps 8-9
# On the ‘Summary of attempt’ screen, note that it now displays ‘Answer saved’:

!image-20250908-065834.png|width=1185,height=790,alt="image-20250908-065834.png"!

Observed behaviour:

The question status is incorrectly flagged as ‘Answer saved’ in the restored course, even when users new to the course make an attempt. This means in the ‘View attempts’ screen, users have these questions flagged as ‘Requires grading’ when in reality, they didn’t answer the question at all and there is only template data present (therefore no need for a Teacher to grade them)

Expected behaviour:

The question status will be ‘Not yet answered’ in all cases where a Student has not inserted any data beyond the template text.

Impact:

When performing course rollovers to create new versions of the course for the next teaching period, Teachers may click into questions thinking they require grading when they have not been answered. Ultimately this results in time wasted during marking.

fields.description:
In [MDL-69877] a new security.txt file, following the information @ [security.txt|https://securitytxt.org/] was introduced.

The security.txt file located in _public/security.txt (or security.txt pre 5.1)_ must be updated regularly, shortly before it expires (defined by the {{Expires}} element within the file).

+*The updates should be made to main, as well as all other security supported Moodle versions that contain security.txt.*+ This means all supported versions have an identical security.txt file (including the same expiry).

This task must only land in the minor release versions that are scheduled for release alongside the relevant major release  (for example if 5.2 is the major release, then 5.1.3 will be one of the minors receiving the update). Therefore, the ideal window for landing this issue is +2-6 weeks prior to release+.

As a minimum, this will involve updating the {{Expires}} value, which needs to be set to *[expected subsequent major release date]* *+ 3 WEEKS*. This provides a small buffer in case the major release is delayed. If any of other details in the security.txt need to be amended, they should also be completed at the same time. We should also check the RFC in case of any changes (see the [Github repo|https://github.com/securitytxt/security-txt] to check if any versions have been released since the previous LMS release).

----

Detailed information (to be modified for each clone of this issue):

* *Branches affected:* main (5.2), 5.1, 5.0, 4.5
* *Expiry (5.3 release + 3 weeks):* 5 October 2026 + 3 weeks =  26 October 2026
* *Commit message:* MDL-XXXXXX core: Update security.txt expiry
* *Other changes:* _... add any further changes required here_

Exact formatted expiry date to use: *2026-10-26T01:00:00.000Z*

How the date format was calculated (in line with the [latest spec|https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-foudil-securitytxt-12#section-3.5.5]):

{{date --date='26 October 2026 01:00' -u +"%FT%H:%M:%S.000Z"}}

----

(This issue is part of the release process, 2 weeks before release, and will be cloned as part of it.)

This task corresponds to point #3 of the [1 week prior release|https://moodledev.io/general/development/process/release#1-week-prior] tasks.

It's achieved semi-automatically using the "{{versions_check_set.sh}}" script available in the [local_ci|https://github.com/moodlehq/moodle-local_ci/blob/main/versions_check_set/versions_check_set.sh] plugin.

# Create a working {{main}} instance local_ci plugin installed. Remove Composer's "vendor" directory and any non-core plugins if you're working on an existing instance.

# Define and export all the env variables required by the script.

* {{$WORKSPACE}}: Path to the directory where test results will be sent ({{/tmp}})
* {{$phpcmd}}: Path to the PHP CLI executable (e.g. {{/usr/bin/php}})
* {{$gitdir}}: Directory containing git repo (the dirroot of the git, working site)
* {{$setversion}}: 10digits (YYYYMMDD00) to set all versions to. Empty = not set. Since Moodle 2.7, it has been agreed to bump to the planned release version for easier automated checks later in stable land.
* {{$setrequires}}: 10 digits (YYYYMMDD00) to set all required values. Empty = default to $setversion. Since Moodle 2.7, it has been agreed to perform the required bump to the current master version (usually an RC one).

# Run the "{{versions_check_set.sh}}" script. If there are errors, they will be reported, and fixing them will be necessary. (look for "{{ERROR}}" in the {{$WORKSPACE/versions_check_set.txt}} file and/or check the exit status of the script)

# Without errors, all the versions, requires, and dependencies will be bumped.

# Commit

# Note that the main version file is NOT updated at all. One extra commit bumping may be necessary (to anything >= requires version).

# Rerun the checker to verify that there are no errors and no more changes are performed.

Note that the checker is also run periodically by the CI server and as part of the "remote_branch_checker," so normally, all the version.php files should be under control.

fields.summary: Add Moodle 5.1.0 upgrade line to all the upgrade.php scripts

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be completed.  Tasks usually refer to work that must be done outside the product. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)

fields.description:
To have it properly detected for the future, it would be great to add to all the upgrade.php scripts some lines like these:

{code:php}// Automatically generated Moodle v5.1.0 release upgrade line.
// Put any upgrade step following this.{code}

exactly before the "{{return true;}}" present in all the scripts.

Normally, it's ok to do that both in the stable (501_STABLE) and the {{main}} branches, so they will allow quickly find where 5.1.0 started and act once we decide future requirements.

But, *when under parallel development, this only can be done in the stable (501_STABLE) branch* as the {{main}} branch already has diverged and can have own upgrade steps not corresponding to the version just released, but to the future version being developed in parallel.

The change can be performed globally with:

{code:java}#!/bin/bash
export rel="5.1.0" && find . -name upgrade.php | \
xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | \
grep '/db/' | \
xargs grep -L "Automatically generated Moodle v${rel} release upgrade" | \
xargs perl -p -i -e 's@( *)(return true;)@\1// Automatically generated Moodle v$ENV{rel} release upgrade line.\n\1// Put any upgrade step following this.\n\n\1\2@s'{code}

*Command to detect* all the upgrade.php files not having those lines:

{code:java}find . -name upgrade.php | xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | grep '/db/' | xargs grep -L 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.0.0 release upgrade'{code}

*Commands to detect* that we have not added the lines to incorrect files:

{code:java}grep -lr 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.1.0 release upgrade' * | grep -v '/db/'
grep -lr 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.1.0 release upgrade' * | xargs grep -L 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade'{code}

*Command to detect* if the lines have been added after a post-release upgrade step. If there are upgrade steps found, verify that all of them were already there the day of the release and have not been introduced later (you can look for differences between the release v5.0.0 and the current {{main}} branch to verify that)

{code:java}export rel="5.1.0" && export ver="202510" &&
find . -name upgrade.php | \
xargs grep -B25 "Automatically generated Moodle v${rel} release upgrade" | \
grep "upgrade_.*_savepoint.*${ver}"{code}

*Important note to integrators*: The sooner this issue is integrated after release, the fewer chances to get the lines put in an incorrect place (that's what the last "command to detect" above tries to avoid. We need to ensure that the lines are *exactly* at the release point (or we may end up deleting upgrade steps incorrectly in the future). So, immediate integration after release (within the on-sync period and ideally before any new upgrade step is added), it the best achievement.

Ciao 🙂
